hooks.text: Astronauts don't float in space because gravity is gone.
Why do astronauts float if gravity is still there?
Earth's gravity is 90% as strong at the space station.

title: Why astronauts float in space
description: Discover the surprising truth about why astronauts float on the International Space Station.

beats.text: Astronauts don't float in space because gravity is gone.
beats.visual: photograph of an astronaut floating inside the International Space Station, 2020

beats.text: At the altitude of the International Space Station, Earth's gravity is roughly ninety percent as strong as it is at the surface.
beats.visual: diagram of Earth's gravity field and International Space Station orbital altitude, 2021
queries: International Space Station orbital altitude diagram

beats.text: So why does the crew experience total weightlessness?
beats.visual: photograph of astronauts working inside the International Space Station module, 2019

beats.text: The answer is that they and their spacecraft are in a continuous state of free fall.
beats.visual: illustration of Newton's cannonball orbital motion showing continuous free fall, 1687

beats.text: The station moves sideways so fast that as it falls toward the planet, the surface curves away beneath it.
beats.visual: graphic showing the orbital path and curvature of Earth beneath a satellite, 2022

beats.text: This means the crew completes one full orbit around Earth approximately every ninety minutes.
beats.visual: photograph of the International Space Station orbiting above Earth's horizon, 2020
queries: International Space Station orbit Earth horizon

beats.text: Because everything falls together, there is no floor pushing back, proving astronauts don't float because gravity is gone.
beats.visual: photograph of an astronaut floating freely in the Destiny laboratory of the ISS, 2018

better_than_last: This episode applies a mystery structure and a direct contradiction hook to maximize early audience retention and build to a clear, looping payoff.
